chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the New York City Council Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics and asks everyone to sign off or silence electronic devices. Staff confirms the chair is ready and hands the meeting over to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff opens the Rules Committee meeting and asks attendees to silence devices

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to the New York City Council votes on committee on rules, privileges, elections, standards, and ethics.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please sign on all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Moving forward, knowing this approach to the days.

chapters.summary: Council Member Sandra Ung welcomes attendees to the meeting of the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics and identifies herself as the committee chair.
chapters.title: Chair Sandra Ung convenes the committee and introduces herself

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to this meeting of the Committee on Rules, Pre-Religious Elections, Standard Ethics.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I am Council Member Sandra Ong, Chair of the Committee.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung recognizes the committee members in attendance, naming Council Member Krishnan, Council Member Lee, Council Member Encarnación, and Minority Leader David Carr.
chapters.title: Chair Ung recognizes committee members present

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Before we begin, I would like to recognize the other members of this committee who are present.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Council Member Krishnan, Lee Akanasion, and Minority Leader David Carr.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung thanks Council to the Committee Amanda DeGrosso and the staff who prepared the hearing, including Chief Ethics Counsel and Public Integrity Unit Director Pearl Moore, Deputy Director Alicia Vassell, and additional attorneys in the Office of the General Counsel.
chapters.title: Chair Ung acknowledges committee counsel and Public Integrity Unit staff

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: I would also like to acknowledge the Council to the Committee, Amanda DeGrosso, and the committee staff that worked on today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Chief Ethics Counsel and Director of Public Integrity Unit, Pearl Moore, Deputy Director of Public Integrity Unit, Alicia Vassell, and the additional attorneys in the Office of the General Counsel who helped to prepare this hearing.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung explains that by letter dated September 29, 2026, the Bronx Democratic County Committee submitted to the Council and the City Clerk a certification recommending Marricka Scott-McFadden for appointment as Commissioner of the Board of Elections.
chapters.title: Chair Ung describes the Bronx Democratic County Committee certification for Marricka Scott-McFadden

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: By the letter dated September 29, 2026, the Bronx Democratic County Committee submitted to the Council,

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Vietis City Clerk, a certification that Marika Scott McFadden is recommended for appointment by the Council as the Commissioner of the Board of Elections.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung states that the committee will vote on the resolution approving the recommendation of Marricka Scott-McFadden for appointment by the Council as Commissioner of the Board of Elections.
chapters.title: Chair Ung announces the vote on the Scott-McFadden appointment resolution

utterances.speaker: Sandra Ung
utterances.text: Today, we will vote on the resolution approving the recommendations of Marika Scott McFadden for the appointment by the Council as the Commissioner of the Board of Elections.

chapters.summary: Chair Ung asks the committee clerk to call the roll for the vote on the Board of Elections commissioner appointment.
chapters.title: Chair Ung directs the clerk to call the roll

chapters.summary: Committee clerk William Martin opens the roll call vote. Chair Ung votes aye, Council Member Krishnan votes aye, and Council Member Lee votes aye, with no response recorded for Council Member Riley.
chapters.title: Clerk William Martin opens the roll call; Ung, Krishnan and Lee vote aye

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: William Martin, committee clerk, roll call vote, committee on rules, privileges, elections, standards, and ethics.

chapters.summary: The clerk continues the roll call, with Council Member Encarnación voting aye and Minority Leader David Carr voting aye. No responses are recorded for Council Members Williams or Banks at this stage.
chapters.title: Encarnación and Carr add aye votes as the clerk continues the roll

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin reports five votes in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, announcing the item is approved by committee. At the chair's request, the roll is held open for absent members.
chapters.title: Committee records five affirmative votes and holds the roll open

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: With a vote of five in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, our item has been approved by the committee, and the roll will be held open at request of the chair.

chapters.summary: With the roll held open, staff confirm no members are online and the room shifts to informal discussion. Council Member Linda Lee notes she also has Parks and Finance committee business and coordinates holding her other votes open while the Rules roll remains open.
chapters.title: Committee pauses while members attend other committee votes

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I have parks and finance, actually, my committee.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, I have to sometimes do both.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Can you hold parks open for me after I do my vote?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: What time is she has a vote too, right?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You were just leading to the first one.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Actually, I don't think, all the controversial votes, I don't think I'm a target.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: They get us mixed up all the time, too.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: They mix up me and Sandra.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: But I think between you, me, and Julie Wan, they mix me up a lot.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: The funny part is when they mix me up for Susan, because I'm like, she's so much better than I am.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Like, I don't know how you can mix her up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: You know, you've got to remind people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: There are layers to that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I've got to think about this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I've got to switch it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I'm glad I was asked to do that one and not this one, though.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, this one would be bad.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, all the votes are here.

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin resumes the continuation roll call for the Committee on Rules and records Council Member Abreu, bringing the vote to six in the affirmative with the roll still open.
chapters.title: Continuation roll call records Council Member Abreu, tally reaches six

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: Continuation roll call, committee and rules, Council Member Abreu.

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: Vote is currently at six and still open.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, just scooch over a little bit and then make room for Ty, you know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: So whichever has form first, I'll just...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: But it's only because I was 25 minutes late to education.

chapters.summary: After a long pause, the clerk continues the roll call and Council Member Chris Banks votes aye. The clerk reports a final vote of seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, with the item approved by committee.
chapters.title: Council Member Banks votes aye, tally rises to seven

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: Final vote is seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions.

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin corrects his earlier statement, clarifying that the roll call is still open and the committee is awaiting remaining members. The meeting then sits in recess for roughly twenty minutes.
chapters.title: Clerk corrects the record: the roll remains open

chapters.summary: After the extended recess, Council Member Nantasha M. Williams votes aye. The clerk formally records her vote in the continuation roll call for the Committee on Rules.
chapters.title: Council Member Nantasha Williams arrives and votes aye

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin announces the final vote of the Committee on Rules: eight in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions. The resolution approving Marricka Scott-McFadden as Commissioner of the Board of Elections is approved by committee.
chapters.title: Final tally of eight affirmative votes approves the Scott-McFadden appointment

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: Continuation roll call, committee on rules, council member Williams.

chapters.summary: With the vote complete, Chair Sandra Ung closes the meeting and adjourns the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics hearing.
chapters.title: Chair Ung adjourns the meeting

utterances.speaker: William Martin
utterances.text: Final vote, Committee on Rules is, excuse me, eight in the affirmative, zero in the negative, no abstentions.

summary: The Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics convened a brief hearing to vote on the Bronx Democratic County Committee's recommendation of Marricka Scott-McFadden as Commissioner of the Board of Elections.
Chair Sandra Ung opened the meeting, recognized members and staff, and described the September 29, 2026 certification from the Bronx County Democratic Committee.
The roll call was held open for roughly 45 minutes as members attended other committee votes, ending with an 8-0 affirmative vote approving the appointment before Chair Ung adjourned.
title: Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics
topic: Marricka Scott-McFadden - Democratic Elections Commissioner for Bronx County
